pool.text: Anthony Henday, an explorer for the Hudson's Bay Company, may have entered the Edmonton area.
Treaty 6 was signed between First Nations and the Crown in the region.
Edmonton established its very first power company to install streetlights along Jasper Avenue.
Edmonton was officially incorporated as a town with a population of 700.
The Edmonton Police Service was founded, later maintaining approximately fourteen hundred officers.
The Journal was established to produce print editions and e-versions in Edmonton.
CKUA began broadcasting music as the first major radio station in the city.
The Edmonton City Centre Airport opened and became Canada's first licensed airfield.
Abdullah Yusuf Ali attended the opening of the new Al-Rashid Mosque in Canada.
CFB Namao began operating as a major air force base in the area.
The University of Alberta established its music department to support music instruction.
The Edmonton Philharmonic and Edmonton Pops orchestras amalgamated to form the modern version.
The Northern Alberta Jubilee Auditorium was constructed for the province's golden jubilee.
Scheduled light rail transit service officially began with subsequent extensions completed over time.
The Sun newspaper was established in Edmonton with a circulation of fifty-five thousand.
Edmonton adopted a European-modelled proof-of-payment fare collection system for transit.
An F4 tornado hit the city and caused the deaths of 27 people.
Jan Reimer became the city's first female mayor after being elected.
City ownership of the telephone service ended when Ed Tel was sold to Telus.
A composting facility was permanently shut down following structural roof inspection findings.
